// Serves every instrument of this process as Prometheus text on its own port, the one the chart names `metrics` and the ServiceMonitor scrapes. import { metrics } from "@opentelemetry/api"; import { PrometheusExporter } from "@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus"; import { MeterProvider } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics"; import { resourceFromAttributes } from "@opentelemetry/resources"; /** For a process with no NodeSDK (the stations service, the MCP gateway): one MeterProvider, registered globally so the instruments in metrics.ts start recording. */ export function startPrometheusMetrics( options: PrometheusMetricsOptions, ): PrometheusMetrics { const port = options.port ?? DEFAULT_METRICS_PORT; const reader = prometheusReader(port); const provider = new MeterProvider({ resource: resourceFromAttributes({ "service.name": options.serviceName }), readers: [reader], }); metrics.setGlobalMeterProvider(provider); console.log(`[otel] ${options.serviceName} metrics on :${port}/metrics`); return { port, stop: () => provider.shutdown() }; } export interface PrometheusMetrics { port: number; stop: () => Promise; } // The OTel SDK of the remote app: traces to Cloud Trace, metrics served to Prometheus on the `metrics` port. Imported FIRST in the entrypoint and started before any instrument is touched. import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node"; import type { SpanExporter } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base"; import { metricsPortFromEnv, prometheusReader, } from "@re-cinq/lore-shared/otel/prometheus-metrics.js"; function httpInstruments(meter: Meter) { return { httpLatency: meter.createHistogram("lore.http.duration_ms", { description: "HTTP request duration in milliseconds", unit: "ms", }), httpRequests: meter.createCounter("lore.http.requests", { description: "Total HTTP requests", }), }; } function stationInstruments(meter: Meter) { return { stationRuns: meter.createCounter("lore.station.runs", { description: "Service station runs, by station and outcome", }), stationLatency: meter.createHistogram("lore.station.duration_ms", { description: "Service station run duration in milliseconds", unit: "ms", }), busDeliveries: meter.createCounter("lore.bus.deliveries", { description: "Bus deliveries this process finished, by event and result", }), busQueueDepth: meter.createObservableGauge("lore.bus.queue_depth", { description: "Deliveries waiting for this process's subscriber", }), }; } function MetricRow({ label, values }: { label: string; values: string[] }) { return ( {label} {values.map((value, i) => ( {value} ))} ); } export function activityRoutes(getPool: () => Pool | null): ServerRoute[] { return [ memoryAuditRoute(getPool), eventsRoute(getPool), jobRunRoute(getPool), activityCountsRoute(getPool), ]; }
--- adr_number: 50 title: "Metrics go to Prometheus and Grafana, installed by terraform" status: in progress date: 2026-10-09 deciders: ["Bogdan Szabo"] domains: [observability, infrastructure, terraform, lore-api, stations, floor, ai-agent-subsystem] --- # ADR-050: Metrics go to Prometheus and Grafana, installed by terraform This ADR records where Lore's numbers live and why: every service serves OpenTelemetry metrics as Prometheus text on its own port, a terraform-installed kube-prometheus-stack scrapes them together with the floor's and the agent controller's `/metrics`, and Grafana behind the Headlamp-style Google gate shows them on dashboards that are built once and name no assembly line. ## Decision - **Instruments are resolved lazily, against the provider registered at record time.** `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts` holds every Lore instrument and looks each up on the current global meter provider, memoized per provider, so a record made after a late registration lands and a record made on a laptop adapter that never registers one costs nothing. - A failed tool call counts as one call and one error. - A request's path is collapsed to its first segments with ids replaced, so a route is one series. - **Every Lore service serves Prometheus text on a `metrics` port**, 9464 by default (`LORE_METRICS_PORT`), through `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus`: lore-api hands the reader to its NodeSDK beside the Cloud Trace exporter, which keeps traces; the stations service and the lore-mcp gateway register one MeterProvider of their own. The Cloud Monitoring metric exporter is gone. - **Each thing worth counting is recorded at exactly one site.** - A service station's run and duration, by station and outcome, where the stations service runs any station by HTTP or from the bus. - A bus delivery's result in the shared drain loop. - The depth of the stations subscriber's queue, read from the deliveries port on every scrape. - A start on the floor, by line and whether it joined an open run, in the one shared `startLine`. - A GitHub delivery, by the bus event it became, in the webhook route. - **Lore's own model calls are metered by decorating the usage sink**, so every provider is covered by one site: calls by provider, model and status; tokens by kind; computed cost in USD. - **Billed spend is a gauge read from the synced invoices**, `lore.billed.cost_usd` by vendor, item and window (today, month to date), from the same two daily tables `/spend` reads, so the two never disagree. ## Context Nothing answered "what is happening on the factory floor" as numbers. lore-api started an OpenTelemetry SDK that pushed metrics to Cloud Monitoring, which nobody opened; the stations service and the lore-mcp gateway started no SDK at all. The floor ([re-cinq/floor](https://github.com/re-cinq/floor)) and the ai-agent-subsystem controller each already served a hand-written Prometheus `/metrics`, but nothing scraped them. Worse, lore-api's own counters had never recorded anything. The OpenTelemetry metrics API, unlike its tracing API, has no proxy meter: an instrument created from `metrics.getMeter()` before a `MeterProvider` is registered is a permanent no-op. `libs/server-core/src/outbound/otel.ts` created its instruments at import time, and the entrypoint imported it before `initOtel()` ran, so `lore.http.requests`, `lore.tool.calls` and the rest were dead from the day they were written. Two Prometheus flavours were weighed. Google Managed Prometheus bills $0.06 per million samples, so it grows with every histogram and label a dashboard asks for. The self-hosted stack on Autopilot bills its pods' requests, about $27 a month, flat: 600m CPU and 1.7 GiB across Prometheus, its operator, kube-state-metrics, Grafana and an oauth2-proxy, plus a 10 Gi disk. GKE's own pod metrics stay free in Cloud Monitoring either way, so Grafana reads those through a Cloud Monitoring datasource.
**metrics-stack/2026-10-09** (memory): Metrics stack (ADR-050) built 2026-10-09 across three repos, four PRs, none applied yet: lore #2652 (OTel → Prometheus exporter on :9464 in lore-api/stations/gateway; new instruments lore.station.*, lore.bus.*, lore.floor.starts, lore.webhook.events, lore.llm.*, lore.billed.cost_usd; instruments resolved lazily because the OTel metrics API has no proxy meter and lore-api's counters had been permanent no-ops since import-time creation), floor #39 (SQL-derived run/visit duration histograms, totals and cost by line_id/node_id/model in metrics-sql.ts), ai-agent-subsystem #271 (histogram kind + controller_runs_completed_total, controller_run_duration_seconds, controller_run_queue_seconds, controller_run_failures_total{kind}; ReconcileEffect carries Decision; ObjectMeta.creationTimestamp; contracts regenerated), lore feat/monitoring-stack (monitoring.tf: kube-prometheus-stack 92.2.0 on Autopilot with node-exporter/control-plane off and kubelet Service in monitoring; Grafana behind oauth2-proxy on the Headlamp Google client with auth.proxy + NetworkPolicy; Grafana GSA for Cloud Monitoring; 5 dashboards: factory overview, assembly line (templated by line label), agent controller, services, spend). Cost chosen: self-hosted ~$27/mo flat vs GMP per-sample. Remaining manual: add Grafana redirect URI to the headlamp OAuth client, tag floor, cut subsystem release + bump controller digest in floor chart, terraform apply from main, verify ingress_controller_namespace (gcloud auth expired during the session). Traps: floor has no prettier (never run it there); re-lint requires spec links on every lore test and ADR status 'in progress' when statements lack links. **session:re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem** (episode) [observed]: The controller now shares how runs end and how long they take through its metrics endpoint. **session:re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem** (episode) [observed]: Monitoring and observability improvements were made this week. **session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: Any Kubernetes cluster can now be connected to the system and monitored through heartbeats and dedicated registration pages. **dod/otto-153-conversation-reader** (memory): DoD for re-cinq/Otto#153 (read-only operator view of an escalated conversation). Spec is specs/support-agent-escalation/spec.md User Story 8 + FR-095..FR-110 + CR-016..CR-028 (all were un-linked). Strategy parallel-change. Committed 3 RED pure tests in apps/api/test/conversationReader.test.ts pointing at not-yet-existing apps/api/src/reader/conversationView.ts (pure (session,escalation)->view) and renderTranscript.ts (view->injected sink): FR-102 (503 turn reads end-to-end: question verbatim + assistant answer + failed toolName + trigger tms_unavailable), FR-108/FR-107 (four roles user/assistant/thinking/tool in array order; ThinkingEntry has NO timestamp per hal-engine ChatSession type, must not render undefined/Invalid Date/NaN/1970), CR-020 (authHeaders authorization/cookie/host never leak into view or transcript). All fail with 'Cannot find module ../src/reader/conversationView.js'. Linked FR-102/FR-108/CR-020 with [validated by](../../apps/api/test/conversationReader.test.ts#Lnn). DEFERRED (documented in .lore/dod.md facets, NOT tested this round): the Mongo access log (conversationAccessLog), readConversation use case, read-conversation CLI, and all GDPR-erasure/EU-AI-Act CRs — because they reuse issue #23's Mongo persistence + erasure primitive, and #23 was NOT on main (no `mongodb` dependency, no conversations collection, no eraseConversation). A red test for them would fail for missing persistence, not the reader's absence. Next pod that has #23 should add those. Env facts: hal-engine installs under apps/api/node_modules/@re-cinq/hal-engine (NOT root); ChatSession/SessionEntry/ThinkingEntry exported from '@re-cinq/hal-engine'; NodeNext so local imports use .js. During this run origin/main advanced and issue #24 escalation code landed (apps/api/src/escalation/*), merged cleanly.

{"answer":"Collection: every Lore service (lore-api, the stations service, and the lore-mcp gateway) serves OpenTelemetry metrics as Prometheus text on a dedicated `metrics` port. The default is 9464, set by `LORE_METRICS_PORT`, and the exporter is `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus`. lore-api hands the Prometheus reader to its NodeSDK, and traces still go to Cloud Trace. The stations service and the gateway have no NodeSDK, so each registers its own MeterProvider through `startPrometheusMetrics`. The Helm charts expose the `metrics` port on the Services, and a ServiceMonitor scrapes it. The Cloud Monitoring metric exporter was removed. A terraform-installed kube-prometheus-stack does the scraping. It also scrapes the floor's and the agent controller's own `/metrics`.

Instruments are defined in `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts` and resolved lazily against the global meter provider. Examples: `lore.http.requests`, `lore.http.duration_ms`, `lore.station.runs`, `lore.station.duration_ms`, `lore.bus.deliveries`, `lore.bus.queue_depth`, `lore.llm.*` (calls, tokens, cost), and `lore.billed.cost_usd`.

Viewing: Grafana in the same stack shows them on dashboards. Grafana sits behind an oauth2-proxy using the Headlamp-style Google login. The dashboards listed in the memory are factory overview, assembly line, agent controller, services and spend. Grafana also reads GKE pod metrics through a Cloud Monitoring datasource. Separately, the web UI analytics page at `/analytics` shows task, latency and token-usage data, and the `lore_get_analytics` MCP tool returns the same data.
